values.note: Maximum spur 40 ft, and not all sites take that length. 9 pull-throughs; double sites hold up to 16 people. recreation.gov lists 25-90 ft by site (25 ft at sites 15 and 25, 30 ft at 24, 34 and 35).

sites.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/riogrande/recreation/thirty-mile-campground ('There are 35 sites. 9 are pull through sites. Not all sites will fit vehicles of this length.') + recreation.gov per-site catalog https://www.recreation.gov/api/search/campsites?fq=asset_id:232338 (35 sites, Max Vehicle Length 25-90), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Water Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day weekend only, and RVs may not fill tanks at the hydrants: arrive with a full tank. Trash service in the summer season only. Firewood sold on site.

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/riogrande/recreation/thirty-mile-campground ('Vault toilets'; 'Water is available in the campground during the summer season, typically Memorial Day Weekend to Labor Day Weekend. Outside of the summer season, potable water is NOT available'; 'Trash service is provided by the concessionaire from Memorial Day to Labor Day.') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232338 (notice 'Please fill your trailer prior to arriving. Trailers are not allowed to fill at any hydrants'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Open year-round but may be inaccessible from snow or spring road closures. Full service (water, trash, host, higher fee) Memorial Day weekend - Labor Day weekend; the 2026 concessionaire season began May 22.

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/riogrande/recreation/thirty-mile-campground ('Open year-round, but may be inaccessible due to snow levels or spring road closures. From Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day weekend, there are higher fees, water, and trash service. During the off-season, there is a reduced fee, no water, and trash must be packed out.'; 'Concessionaire operations for the 2026 season will begin May 22nd.'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: 28 of 35 sites reservable (recreation.gov or 1-877-444-6777), at least 4 days and up to 6 months ahead; 7 first come. Weekend reservations need 2 nights, holiday weekends 3. Off-season all sites are first come. A reserved site not occupied by check-out time the day after arrival is forfeited.

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/riogrande/recreation/thirty-mile-campground ('Reservations must be made at least 4 days ahead of arrival and can be made up to 6 months in advance for standard sites.'; 'Of the 35 campsites: 28 are reservable, 7 are first come, first served.'; 'Campground is currently in off season ... All sites are first-come, first-served.') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232338 (rules reservationCutOff 4, minWeekendStay 2, minHolidayWeekendStay 3, maxStay 14 rolling 30 days; notice on unoccupied reservations) + /rates (Peak Season 2026-05-22 to 2026-09-07), read 2026-10-28

values.note: $29 a single site in the summer season (6 people, 1 vehicle; $10 a night per extra person or second vehicle), $58 a double; $10 a night in the off-season (no water, trash or host). Cash or check at the fee box.

fees.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/riogrande/recreation/thirty-mile-campground ('Single Site: $29 per night'; 'Double Site: $58 per night'; 'Single Site: $10 per night (during shoulder season)'; 'Please be prepared to pay with cash or check.') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232338/rates (Peak Season 2026-05-22 to 2026-09-07 and 2027-05-28 to 2027-09-06: STANDARD NONELECTRIC $29, double $58) + notices (6 people/1 vehicle, $10 extras), read 2026-10-28

note: Rio Grande NF, ~11 mi west on FR 520 off Hwy 149, ~9,300 ft, ~1 mi below Rio Grande Reservoir in a wooded meadow between the Rio Grande and Grizzly Creek. Trailheads to the Weminuche Wilderness (Grizzly Creek #814, Weminuche Creek #818); no horse trailers in the campground (stock unloading area 3/4 mi east on FR 520). Concessionaire-run. --Claude
summary: FS page + recreation.gov (232338) API/rates/catalog: confirmed 35 sites, 9 pull-throughs, vault toilets, seasonal water, reservable with 7 FCFS. Changed season year_round false -> true (FS: 'Open year-round'); fees 29/29 -> 10/29 (off-season $10). Added max 40 ft (FS), booking detail (4-day cutoff, 6-month window, 2/3-night weekend/holiday minimums, 14 nights, reservation season), fees checked 2027. Note cleaned of field facts. Riverview kept.
flags: Phone: none stored. Divide Ranger District (719) 657-3321 (FS page contact). recreation.gov lists the concessionaire (PMC, 719-658-0829, 'For facility specific information, please call (805) 434-1996'). Suggest 719-657-3321.

Length: FS 'Maximum spur length is 40 feet. Not all sites will fit vehicles of this length.' recreation.gov's catalog lists 25-90 ft (86 and 90 at pull-throughs 4 and 7, 80 at 12; 25 ft at sites 15 and 25). Recorded the FS 40; catalog figures over it conflict. Over 23 ft, so no criteria problem; avoid 15 and 25.

Fee page oddity: FS lists 'Single Site with Hookup: $34 per night', but recreation.gov says 'There are no electric site hook-ups at this facility' and the catalog has no electric sites (same Rio Grande boilerplate seen at sibling campgrounds). Ignored; hookups electric 0 kept.
Minimum stay: recreation.gov rules minWeekendStay 2 and minHolidayWeekendStay 3 recorded as rules (a 2-night weekend minimum, under the 3+ outside-weekends drop rule).

Road: the Rio Grande NF conditions page (updated Oct 28, 2026) lists the October 22-23 flood damage; FR 520 (Rio Grande Reservoir Road) is NOT among the damaged roads (Divide RD lists FSR 410, 380, 390, 430, 438). A previous batch (p3-186) quoted the Divide road table for FR 520: 'Open'; 'Summer: Passenger car accessible to Lost Trail Trailhead. Beyond Lost Trail, high clearance and 4x4 required' - Lost Trail is past the reservoir, beyond this campground. No closure.
Pin 37.72259,-107.25709 (= FS coordinates) is 95 m from the catalog centroid and 17 m from the nearest site (1, near the entrance/trailhead parking). OK.

Waterfront (stored riverview, kept): the Rio Grande here is ~15-20 m wide, along the north edge. The nearest sites to it, 28-29, sit ~45-50 m back across the open meadow with the campground road between, and 24-26 in the NE corner are ~35 m back through spruce with another site between. So it fails the open-apron and distance tests for an on-water value (and by size it would be creekside, not riverfront). Grizzly Creek on the east is a few metres wide under continuous spruce, ~50 m from sites 13-17: no frontage, no view. The open meadow gives sites 28-30 a view of the river: riverview stands.
